topic: Parallel execution - concurrency limits, batching, case studies

claims.claim: Claude Code has a 10-concurrent-Task cap: if the main agent fires 15 Task calls, 10 run concurrently and 5 queue FIFO (batch-not-pipe).
Safe parallel conditions (all three required): 3+ genuinely unrelated tasks; no shared file/resource state; clear file-ownership boundaries per agent.
Sequential triggers (any of these = do not parallelize): task dependencies; shared file writes; unclear scope/overlapping responsibility.
Sweet spot: 2-5 parallel agents. Above 5 coordination overhead dominates. Above 10 rarely beats focused single session.
Anthropic C compiler case study (Feb 5 2026): 16 agents, $20,000 cost, 2 billion input tokens + 140 million output tokens, ~2000 sessions, 2 weeks, Opus 4.6.
C compiler project used git-based lock files in current_tasks/ directory for task claiming - a file-lock is the concurrency primitive for Agent Teams task claims.

Time blindness anti-pattern: the orchestrator does not experience wall-clock time, can let parallel agents run 30+ minutes on wrong paths without noticing. Mitigation: explicit check-ins, TeammateIdle hooks, Monitor tool.
Parallel output is a token flood risk for main context: 5 agents each returning 2k-token summaries = 10k of incoming context in one synchronization point. Orchestrator must summarize-of-summaries.
Batch-not-pipe scheduling: tasks queue in FIFO and run when a slot opens; there is no streaming concurrency adjustment. Send 15 at once, get 10 running and 5 waiting.
Weekly rate limits: on Max plan, ~10 hours of heavy parallel use hits weekly quota; explicit model routing (Haiku extractors) extends effective time 3-5x.
Agent Teams shared task list provides built-in coordination: pending/in-progress/completed states + dependencies. Avoids manual orchestrator bookkeeping.
Task dependencies in Agent Teams: a pending task with unresolved dependencies cannot be claimed until deps complete; unblocking happens automatically.
Recommended task count per teammate: 5-6 tasks - keeps teammates productive without excessive context switching.
Parallel code review is the canonical 'safe parallel' use case: each reviewer applies a distinct lens (security / performance / tests) without file conflicts.
Debate-style parallel investigation (5 agents, each assigned a competing hypothesis, instructed to disprove peers) fights anchoring bias in root-cause analysis.

conflicts_flagged.description: Some community guides suggest 10+ parallel agents for exploration; Anthropic and most practitioners cap at 5. 10-concurrent hard cap is separate from recommended sweet spot.
conflicts_flagged.resolution_hint: Distinguish technical cap (10) from optimal range (2-5).

gaps_flagged.description: No published performance data on token throughput at different concurrency levels.
C compiler project did not publish the full orchestration graph - task decomposition patterns inferred from narrative.
